audit.source: czlonkowski/fables @ 914a31c6f6efab0450def55d218dfa16cb308c16 (2026-09-07, branch main, shallow clone; no tags present in clone)
audit.author: Romuald Członkowski (@czlonkowski, aiadvisors.pl) — sole author on all manifests, LICENSE and the single clone commit; identity/reputation NOT independently verified (network restricted)
audit.purpose: A prompt-only delegation protocol for a premium-model session ("plan big, execute small"): a gate for deciding when bulk reading should be fanned out, five workload shapes, a worker-brief format (SUB-QUESTION/SCOPE/REPORT/DON'T), model-tier selection, premise verification, and a bundled read-only `worker` subagent pinned to Sonnet that returns distilled findings with evidence pointers.
files_reviewed: evals/fixtures/eval-1/sync.py (only script in repo; eval fixture, outside the plugin)
directory listing of the whole clone (32 tracked files) — no package.json, no lockfile, no pyproject/requirements, no install script, no hooks, no MCP config
targeted greps across plugins/ for curl|wget|eval|exec|subprocess|postinstall|.ssh|.env|sudo|rm -rf|--dangerously|chmod|api_key|bash -c and for mcpServers|hooks|allowed-tools|Bash(
audit.permissions: Plugin declares no permission block, no allowed-tools, no hooks, no MCP servers, no settings changes. The only tool grant in the package is the bundled agent's front matter: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch`, `model: sonnet` (worker.md:4-5). Everything else is natural-language instruction to the host model; installing it grants no new capability by itself, but it does instruct the host to use the Agent/subagent tool for fan-out.
audit.network_access: No network calls in the package itself (no curl/wget/fetch/http client anywhere under plugins/fable-orchestrator). Indirect only: the bundled worker agent is granted WebFetch and WebSearch, so spawned workers can fetch arbitrary URLs when a brief tells them to (SKILL.md:54-55 "web research" shape). README links are informational and were not followed.
audit.filesystem_access: No file writes, no path manipulation, no installer. Worker agent has Read/Grep/Glob only — read-only, scoped by the brief ("Stay inside the brief's scope", worker.md:22-24). No reads of ~/.ssh, .env, credential stores, or any absolute system path anywhere in the package.
audit.shell_commands: None. No Bash tool grant, no shell snippets, no install/postinstall step in the fable-orchestrator plugin. (Note: the sibling `fable-advisor` plugin in the same repo DOES shell out to `claude -p ...`; it is out of scope here and must not be installed as part of this decision.)

security_findings.finding: Package is entirely Markdown + one JSON manifest — no executable code, no dependencies, no lockfile, no install/postinstall hook, no MCP server, no hooks. Automated grep for the standard dangerous patterns (curl|bash, wget+exec, eval/exec, subprocess, sudo, rm -rf, ~/.ssh, .env reads, --dangerously-skip-permissions, force push) returned zero hits inside the plugin. Attack surface is prompt content only.

Prompt-injection laundering surface: workers are granted WebFetch/WebSearch and read untrusted web/log/file content, while the coordinator is explicitly told to trust their distilled reports — 'Don't re-read what a worker read', 'Spot-check narrowly, not broadly'. Injected instructions in fetched content could reach the coordinator as an authoritative-looking 'finding' with no raw-source review. The worker prompt does require evidence pointers and verified-vs-inferred separation, which mitigates but does not remove this.
security_findings.location: SKILL.md:133-140 (Trusting the reports); worker.md:4 (tools incl. WebFetch/WebSearch)

security_findings.finding: Instructional pressure against self-verification: on worker failure the skill says to re-assign the same brief and 'resist' reading the material yourself, and to rewrite the brief 'rather than escalating the reading to yourself'. Combined with the trust-the-reports rule, a session could accept two degraded reports without ever inspecting the source. This is a cost-optimization instruction, not malicious, but it weakens the verification posture our roles require.

The only script in the repository (evals/fixtures/eval-1/sync.py) accepts an API key via --api-key argv and POSTs base64 file contents to a user-supplied URL. It is a deliberately imperfect eval fixture used as reading material, is not part of the fable-orchestrator plugin, is never referenced or executed by the skill, and was not run during this audit. No exfiltration risk from installing the plugin; noted only so it is not mistaken for skill code.

No release tag or signed release available in the clone (shallow, tags not fetched); plugin.json is version 0.1.0 and marketplace.json 0.6.0. Pinning is therefore only possible by commit hash 914a31c6f6efab0450def55d218dfa16cb308c16, which is verified present in .git/packed-refs for origin/main.

quality_findings: Well-written, internally consistent protocol: explicit gate, explicit non-use cases ('When NOT to split'), explicit user-override clause (SKILL.md:152-153), and a worker contract that demands evidence pointers instead of raw dumps. Prose quality is high and the scope is narrow — no scope creep into generation or decisions.

Honest self-reporting: the README states that the ~2.5x cheaper / 3x faster / 84-98% figures are Anthropic's cookbook numbers on a web-research workload, not re-measured in Claude Code, and that the orchestrator evals are 'still planned' (README.md:310-312, 415-418). The SKILL.md itself repeats those figures three times without the same caveat, so the skill text reads more confident than the evidence behind it.

Author's own trigger benchmark reports near-zero recall for this skill — it rarely auto-fires — and the documented workaround is to hardcode a line into CLAUDE.md (README.md:390-413). Value therefore depends on us editing CLAUDE.md, which is itself a change worth deciding deliberately.
Hardcoded, dated pricing ($10/$50 per MTok, '5x Sonnet, 10x Haiku, as of 2026-07') in both SKILL.md:8-9 and README.md:302-303 will silently rot and start feeding stale cost claims into sessions.

The SKILL.md front-matter `description` is a single ~1,400-character block (SKILL.md:3). Some hosts cap skill descriptions around 1024 characters; verify it loads without truncation before relying on it.

Repo maturity signals are thin: single author, version 0.1.0, no CI, no automated tests (evals/ are JSON scenario specs, not an executable suite), no CHANGELOG, no SECURITY policy, no releases/tags visible. GitHub stars/forks/contributors could not be checked (network restricted), so Tier 1 popularity and maintenance criteria are unverified rather than met.

README documents `.agents/skills/...` relative symlinks as present 'in this checkout' (README.md:44-45, 133-134); no `.agents` directory exists in the 32-file clone. Minor doc/repo mismatch — worth confirming the packaged layout matches the docs before install.

Architecture fit is imperfect: the skill assumes Claude-native subagents pinned to Sonnet/Haiku, while our system runs workers as Codex processes per .ai/config.json and AGENTS.md, and our common rules forbid the Agent tool unless a skill or CLAUDE.md authorizes it. Adopting this skill effectively changes that default and overlaps with roles we already have.
audit.why_this_one: It is the only candidate that is pure prompt text with zero executable surface — nothing to install, nothing to run, trivially reversible by deleting one directory — while still encoding a concrete, reviewable delegation contract (brief format, tier selection, premise verification, anti-over-splitting rule) rather than vague advice. It also derives from a Tier 0 source pattern (Anthropic's plan-big-execute-small cookbook) and ships a read-only worker agent whose tool grant is minimal and auditable in four lines.
alternatives_considered: Write an internal skill in .claude/skills/ (~60-80 lines) implementing the same gate + brief format against OUR worker model from .ai/config.json — no external dependency, no trust question, no Claude-subagent assumption. Strongest alternative; our role rules already prefer an internal sub-100-line skill over a doubtful external one.

Use Anthropic's plan-big-execute-small cookbook directly (anthropics/claude-cookbooks, Tier 0) as the reference and adapt it ourselves — authoritative source, but it is a notebook, not a packaged skill, so it needs the same authoring work as the internal option.

Install nothing: our orchestrator already defines manager/worker roles, task decomposition in .ai/TASKS.json, and run logging in .ai/RUNS/, which covers much of the fan-out discipline this skill teaches.

The sibling plugins in the same repo (fable-advisor, astra-advisor, astra-orchestrator) were explicitly NOT evaluated for installation and must not be bundled in: fable-advisor shells out to `claude -p` and astra-advisor to `codex exec`, which is a materially larger and separate audit.
audit.recommendation_reason: No security blocker was found — the package contains no executable code, no dependencies, no install hooks, no shell, no network calls, and the bundled worker is read-only; the two low findings (report-trust weakening verification, WebFetch-borne injection reaching the coordinator) are design characteristics, not malice. But it does not reach Tier 1: single author, v0.1.0, no CI/tests/tags/changelog/security policy, and popularity and maintainer-reputation signals were unverifiable offline, so it lands at Tier 2 (promising but unproven), which per our rules cannot be manager-approved. Independently, adoption is an architecture decision for BRAIN: it presumes Claude-native subagents pinned to Sonnet/Haiku while our workers are Codex per .ai/config.json, it only fires reliably if we add a line to CLAUDE.md, and it overlaps with roles we already have — so an internal sub-100-line equivalent is a live and cheaper option. If BRAIN approves, conditions: install ONLY plugins/fable-orchestrator (never the advisor siblings), pin to commit 914a31c6f6efab0450def55d218dfa16cb308c16 (no tag exists; never track main), record a DEC-* ADR for the Agent-tool/CLAUDE.md change, keep spot-checking of load-bearing worker claims mandatory in our wrapper despite SKILL.md:133-140, strip or date-guard the hardcoded pricing lines, confirm GitHub stats and the ~1,400-char description limit once network is available, and re-audit by diff on any update.
